stage1.impression: A tidy, believable layout of a warm timber bar at night, but it reads as a competent architectural render rather than a photograph. The lantern's face is a flat, evenly lit pair of veneer doors that look like a lift, the amber band reads as front-lit corrugated board rather than glowing acrylic, and the materials (terrazzo like fine carpet noise, uniform slat repeat, perfect CG glasses) are too clean. There is no EARF speaker and no saturated colour anywhere in frame, and no sign of life, so a magazine would see a generic, empty, nicely toned bar, not a specific place.

blocking_9: The frame needs a reason to exist: either the lantern's porch shown open or ajar with the lit Ember Tropos pair or Mother EARF readable through it, or the camera reframed so one EARF product is the single saturated colour and the hero.

The acrylic band must read as lit cast acrylic: an internal glow with bright polished fin edges, not front-lit slats (band region lum_median above 110, with lum_p95 at least 60 above lum_p5 from edge glow, not from the haze beam).
The porch doors must stop reading as a flat lift: a raking light with a falloff across them and visible oak grain, not an even wash.
Signs of life: a figure (motion-blurred), a coat on the banquette, a record out of its sleeve on the counter or table; the room is currently a showroom.

Material realism at 1:1: terrazzo chips at a real scale (currently reads as carpet or noise), quartzite with a visible vein and a soft reflection of the pendant, oak with real variation across the slats instead of an identical repeat.
No render artefacts: no fireflies on the band, no straight haze shafts from unseen fixtures cutting across the dark ceiling.

defects.what: The acrylic band reads as corrugated card or metal lit from the front; no internal glow and no glowing fin edges. RGB median 135/76/43, delta E 2000 of 28 against a warm amber #D98A2B.
Two fireflies (bright blue-white specks) on the band, at about (676,138) and (762,155).
A straight, hard-edged haze shaft from an off-frame fixture crosses the ceiling and the band diagonally; it reads as a CG volumetric beam.
A second haze shaft at the top right, same problem.
The porch doors are an evenly lit flat veneer (lum_median 60, range 78) with a centre seam; they read as lift doors or a wardrobe, not a sound lock with depth.
The blackened steel strip on the porch's right reads as an empty black gap (edge step 32 over 4 px), with no sheen or patina.
A grey plastic-looking box on the porch post (keypad or switch) is the brightest neutral on the face and draws the eye.
The slatted baffle is an identical repeat of slats with no variation in tone or grain; a hard diagonal shadow wedge on its left half (about 300-400, 330-560) has no visible caster.
The pendant's shade is near-white (p95 227) and is the only cool-white object in a 2700 K room; it reads as a stock model.
The quartzite top reads as matte dark grey laminate; no vein, no reflection of the pendant or bottles.
The terrazzo counter face and floor read as fine noise or carpet at 1:1, not chips in a honed ground.
The foreground tables are a dark, unlit block (lum_median 23) with four identical copies of one table; the right third of the frame is dead.
The right wall is a blank dark plane (lum_median 17) with no texture, practical or object.
No people, no coats, no records out; no saturated EARF colour anywhere in frame.

changes.problem: The frame has no hero: no EARF product and no saturated colour are visible, so the picture is a generic bar.

evidence.measured: The porch is closed; the only warm colour is the band (RGB 135/76/43); nothing in frame reads as Ember tint.

change.setting: the porch door's state (a small prop or set state) and camera
change.to: one porch leaf open about 40 deg (or the opening clear), with the camera's target moved so the opening sits on the right third and the lit Ember Tropos or Mother EARF reads through it

changes.expected: A small, bright, saturated Ember shape seen through the dark porch: the one colour in the frame and the place the eye goes after the band.

changes.problem: The acrylic band does not glow; it is lit from the front by the room and reads as corrugated card.

evidence.measured: lum_median 86, p95 138; profile along x flat at 78 to 111, the peak caused by the haze shaft, not the band; delta E 28 to an amber.

change.to: 0.35, with the band's emission 2200 K so the Smoke fins turn amber; keep the fins' edges polished

changes.expected: A self-lit, even amber band with brighter fin edges, the brightest large surface in the frame but not clipped.

changes.problem: The porch face is evenly washed and reads as flat lift doors.

evidence.measured: lum_median 60, lum_range 78, with no top-to-bottom gradient beyond the downlight's hotspot.

change.to: 1 x area 1.2 W/m2, 2400 K, moved to a narrow strip at the porch's head so it rakes down the oak; the route fill from 0.1 to 0.04 W/m2

changes.expected: The porch reads with depth and grain: brighter at its head, falling off towards the floor, with the leaf edges catching light.

changes.problem: Straight volumetric shafts from unseen fixtures cut across the dark ceiling and the band.

evidence.measured: A diagonal shaft visible across the ceiling (region lum_p95 80 against a ceiling median of 15).

change.to: 0.002 per meter, or exclude the off-frame downlights from the volume

changes.expected: The ceiling stays a soft, even dark with no hard beams; the atmosphere shows only as a slight glow around the practicals.

changes.problem: The room is empty and staged, a showroom rather than a bar in use.

evidence.measured: people: 0 figures; no coats, records or open bottles.

change.to: 2 figures (a bartender behind the counter, one guest on the banquette), motion-blurred, faces never shown; a coat over the banquette's back, a record out of its sleeve on the near table, a bottle open on the counter

changes.expected: The frame reads as a working listening bar at night, fuller and warmer.

changes.problem: The right third (tables and banquette) is a dead dark block with four identical tables.

change.to: 4 x spot 60.0 W, 22.0 deg, aimed at the table tops so each makes a pool with dark between

changes.expected: Pools of light on each table and glass, the leather's sheen readable, dark between the pools.

changes.problem: The terrazzo and quartzite read as noise and laminate at 1:1.

evidence.measured: Counter top lum_range 82 with no veining; the floor and counter face show uniform fine speckle at the pixel scale.

change.setting: the terrazzo's chip size and ground tone; the glass's reflection; the quartzite finish
change.from: fine chips on a dark ground; matte top
change.to: chips of 8 to 20 mm on a mid-warm grey ground, honed with a low sheen; quartzite honed with a soft reflection of the pendant and bottles

changes.expected: Chips readable as stone at their real size; a soft streak of reflected light along the bar top.

changes.problem: Fireflies on the band and a cool-white pendant shade break the render's credibility.

evidence.measured: Two isolated blue-white specks; the pendant shade at about RGB 142/132/122, p95 227, the only neutral-white in the room.

change.setting: render clamp and the pendant's shade
change.to: clamp 2.0 (indirect only), samples 512; the shade's glow warmed to 2400 K and dimmed so its p95 sits near 200

changes.expected: No fireflies; the pendant reads as a warm practical in the same family as the band.

out_of_scope.request: Replace the plastic-looking keypad on the porch post or give it a blackened steel plate.
out_of_scope.why: It is part of the porch as drawn; the owner should decide whether it stays.

out_of_scope.request: Break the identical repeat of the four foreground tables (different tops or a mix of heights).
out_of_scope.why: The furniture layout is fixed with the architecture.

out_of_scope.request: Give the slatted baffle irregular slat widths or visible joints.
out_of_scope.why: The baffle's design is fixed; only the oak's tone and finish may change (a per-slat tone variation within the oak is in scope).
